X-WAM leverages the strong visual priors of pretrained video diffusion models by imagining the future world through predicting multi-view RGB-D videos, and obtains spatial information efficiently through a lightweight structural adaptation: replicating the final few blocks of the pretrained Diffusion Transformer into a dedicated depth prediction branch for the reconstruction of future spatial information.

## Being-H0.7: A Latent World-Action Model from Egocentric Videos

Being-H0.7 is a latent world-action model pretrained from large-scale egocentric videos. The model was published on April 14, 2026.

### Key Technical Approach

Instead of predicting future frames, Being-H0.7 introduces a small set of learnable latent queries between the multimodal context and the action tokens, reframing world modeling as learning compact, control-relevant predictive factors and avoiding the training and inference inefficiencies of image-then-act pipelines.

The model uses an efficient dual-branch formulation with hidden-state alignment and lightweight regularization to prevent latent collapse, enabling scalable pretraining on large-scale egocentric videos.

### Training Data and Scale

Being-H0.7 is trained on 200,000 hours of egocentric human videos together with 15,000 hours of robot demonstrations.

### Performance

In simulation, Being-H0.7 achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance across six benchmarks, and in the real world, it was evaluated on three robot platforms across 12 challenging tasks covering dynamic scenes, physical reasoning, motion reasoning, long-horizon execution, and generalization, leading all five ability-oriented suites.

With latency-aware universal asynchronous chunking, Being-H0.7 variants operate in the 3–4 ms/step regime without adding the burden of test-time future generation.

## Overview

ShengShu Technology announced Motubrain, a World Action Model that replaces multiple task-specific systems with a single, unified model that functions as a robotic brain for the physical world.

## Architecture and Attention Mechanism

MotuBrain uses an H-bridge attention design to balance cross-modal interaction and efficiency, while supporting flexible multiview inputs through view-dependent 3D RoPE offsets. 

MotuBrain introduces a three-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture with a text stream, a video stream, and an action stream. Action queries attend to the cached video/text keys and values together with their own action keys and values.

## Key Capabilities

DreamZero is a World Action Model built on a pretrained video diffusion backbone. Unlike VLAs, WAMs learn physical dynamics by predicting future world states and actions, using video as a dense representation of how the world evolves.

Video-only demonstrations from other robots or humans yield a relative improvement of over 42% on unseen task performance with just 10-20 minutes of data. Unified World Model (UWM) is a multimodal diffusion transformer that uses separate diffusion timesteps for actions and videos to flexibly learn policies, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, and video prediction models from both robot and video data.

A UWM integrates an action diffusion process and a video diffusion process within a unified transformer architecture, where independent diffusion timesteps govern each modality. ## TACA: Temperature-Adjusted Cross-Modal Attention

TACA (Temperature-Adjusted Cross-modal Attention) is a parameter-efficient method that dynamically rebalances multimodal interactions through temperature scaling and timestep-dependent adjustment.

### Key Components

The approach introduces two key innovations: (1) modality-specific temperature scaling to mitigate cross-attention suppression, and (2) timestep-dependent adjustments to cross-modal interactions.

### Early vs. Late Denoising Steps

The method treats different denoising phases differently. The approach substantially amplifies the attention directed toward the text in the early steps. A piecewise function separates the layout formation and detail refinement phases, with early steps (i.e., large t) focusing on visual details when self-attention dominates.

When combined with LoRA fine-tuning, TACA significantly enhances text-image alignment on the T2I-CompBench benchmark with minimal computational overhead.

### Implementation

TACA introduces no new learnable parameters, with the temperature scaling implemented via a simple element-wise operation during attention computation.

The paper was accepted at ICCV 2025, and the code is publicly available at https://github.com/Vchitect/TACA.
